newsitem.title: CHILE: Edelnor to buy Atacama natgas.
newsitem.headline: Edelnor to buy Atacama natgas.

text.p: Power utility Empresa Electrica del Norte Grande SA, or Edelnor, plans to buy natural gas from the Atacama pipeline due to stretch from northern Argentina to Chile, the company said.

Edelnor, controlled by Atlanta-based Southern Co, became the first major client for the Atacama project due to come onstream in 1999. "We've taken a position on the Atacama pipeline because we are committed to the economic development of northern Chile, and we want to continue being a low-cost electricity provider," said an Edelnor statement quoting General Manager Mark Lynch.

But the statement said it "remains to be demonstrated" that the Atacama pipeline, being built by U.S. firm CMS Energy Corp and Chile's Empresa Nacional de Electricidad SA, or Endesa, is "viable given current demand levels and the distance that the pipeline will have to cover from northern Argentina to the coast of Chile."

Edelnor opened its Mejillones plant near the northern city of Antofagasta in April and is building a second plant nearby to be known as Mejillones II, which it will fuel with Atacama natgas, said the statement.

The $350 million Atacama project, whose "open season" for clients ends Wednesday, will carry natural gas from the Argentine province of Salta to Chile's copper-rich north by 1999, one of two major projects to bring Argentine natgas to Chile.

Endesa joined the project last month after the departure of Canada's Nova Corp, which is due to finish another natgas pipeline, known as GasAndes, from the Argentine province of Mendoza to Santiago by early 1998 with Chilgener SA.

Chilgener plans to finish its project for electrical transmission lines stretching from Argentina to northern Chile in 1999, raising the prospect of more energy supply than current demand can sustain in northern Chile, analysts have said.
Both the Atacama project and Chilgener's project would supply power to the Norte Grande Interconnected System, the power grid for the country's fast-growing north.
